title: Art as Infrastructure at the Medina Triennial
summary: The inaugural edition of the sprawling yet rigorous exhibition examines the labor, regulation, extraction, and repair of our shared systems.

title: Who Stole the Guggenheim’s Picasso?
summary: The museum sues to retrieve a piece stolen in 1961, Dean Millien’s aluminum-foil animal sculptures, and more.

title: Taiwanese Artists Accuse South Korea’s Gwangju Biennale of Censorship
summary: The Biennale’s decision to exclude “Taiwan” from the pavilion’s official name “is a threat to freedom of expression and the global art community,” the artists said.

title: Why Won’t Britain Return Looted Gold to Ghana?
summary: In “The African Kingdom of Gold,” Barnaby Phillips explores how British colonial forces plundered the Asante people and expertly traces the stolen artifacts’ afterlives in museum storage.

title: School of Visual Arts Faculty “Blindsided” by Course Cuts Amid $22M Deficit
summary: The SVA faculty union called on leadership at the New York institution to work with its community to address the impact of budget reductions.

title: Shu Lea Cheang Gives Trans Artists the Wings to Fly
summary: The filmmaker invites visitors to move and reposition the screens in her four-channel video at Leslie-Lohman, an ever-evolving mosaic of trans performances and dreamscapes.

title: Halloween Comes Early With New Kristi Noem Statue in South Dakota
summary: The bronze sculpture depicts the notorious former Secretary of Homeland Security in full “ICE Barbie” gear with her favorite horse, regrettably named “Iceman.”

title: Mary Heilmann Dies at 86
summary: Plus: Dean Millien's aluminum-foil animal world, another museum heist in Europe, and the architect leading a new Chinese vernacular.

title: Mary Heilmann, Painter of Irreverent Abstractions, Dies at 86
summary: “My inspiration for art doesn’t really come from the history of painting,” the artist told Hyperallergic in a 2013 interview, “it comes from the community of art as it is now.”

title: NYC Culture Commissioner Diya Vij Appoints Bryan Joseph Lee as Deputy
summary: The cultural strategist and producer will work alongside the curator and commissioner at the Department of Cultural Affairs.

title: Dean Millien’s Aluminum-Foil Animal World
summary: A highlight of “Greater New York” at MoMA PS1, the artist’s remarkable sculptures made from the humble household material continue a practice he began as a child in Brooklyn.

title: RISD MFA Students Paint Through the Heartbreak
summary: Each painting is like an island awash with yearning, sending out a lighthouse signal into a fractured world.

title: Priceless Renaissance Paintings Stolen From Italian Museum
summary: Authorities say thieves made off with four artworks by Sicilian master Antonello da Messina in under five minutes.

title: The Architect Shaping a New Chinese Vernacular
summary: Pritzker-winner Wang Shu’s design for the Ningbo Historic Museum reconciles China’s nostalgia with its desire for a shiny, avant-garde future.

title: Deepen Your Creative Practice at Vermont Studio Center
summary: Full and partial fellowships available for artists and writers
